<reflection>
- The first experiment yielded very similar negative log-likelihood (NLL) values for almost all models (around -23.6 to -24.0), with only M5 showing a significantly worse fit. 
- This indicates that under standard conditions with moderate substrate and low catalyst, the kinetic profiles of these mechanisms are highly degenerate. 
- The aim of establishing a baseline was achieved, but to break this degeneracy, we must introduce conditions that explicitly trigger the unique pathways of the different models (e.g., product presence, high catalyst concentration).
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
To differentiate the remaining models, we need to probe specific interactions that were inactive or weak in the first experiment. By introducing a high initial product concentration (P=0.5), we can strongly activate product-inhibition or product-deactivation pathways (M12, M17). Simultaneously, increasing the catalyst concentration to its maximum (cat=0.20) will amplify second-order catalyst interactions, such as dimerization (M2, M3) or bimolecular deactivation (M13, M18, M19). A moderate substrate concentration (S=1.0) will significantly lower the S/cat ratio compared to the first run (from 40 down to 5). This shifts the steady-state distribution between free catalyst and the catalyst-substrate complex, which will help distinguish between deactivation/inhibition mechanisms that depend on free 'cat' (M9, M11, M12) versus those that depend on 'catS' (M14, M16, M17).
</hypothesis>
